findings.text: the line search never treats the incumbent state as a trial: `better` accepts the first valid trial unconditionally via `(trials == 0)`, so when every halving still reads worse than the current state the lane moves to the best trial rather than staying put, and the fresh residual increases; base took the full step unconditionally so this is not a regression, but it is a weaker guarantee than the docstring's 'retaining the best valid trial' invites a reader to assume.

`reads + trials` counts trials per lane, so the companion read_batch that every while-loop iteration performs for lanes that are not themselves pending is uncounted, and SolveResult.reads no longer equals the number of fresh reads; the invariant asserted at tests/test_bank_solve_driver.py:287 (`reads == steps + 1`) happens to hold only because that fixture never backtracks twice.

the provenance probe runs `python -c` without `-P`, so the working directory (the head worktree) precedes PYTHONPATH and a base-arm log's header names the head module; stall-base-test_bank_solve_cycle.log:2 prints the worktree support_read.py for a run whose behaviour is the base arm (0 unfreezes against head 2), so only the outcome distinguishes the arms and the header cannot.

the added per-lane halving search at nova/equilibrium/support_read.py:1692 duplicates the repository's bounded dyadic backtracking search `_damped_scale`, which solves.test_driver's cold Newton path already uses; the new search is per-lane and validity-aware, but it does not extend or wrap that owner, so this is a duplication rather than an extension.
